note: Water and tide (docs/07). Meters, seconds, Y-up, mean sea level 0. The live simulation is visual only and runs on real seconds; the tide is analytic and read at display time for the look and at world time for the hourly tick.

tide.note: level(t) = A(t) cos(2 pi t / periodH + phase), A(t) = amplitudeM (1 + springNeap cos(4 pi moonPhase)). phaseH shifts high water in game hours.

sim.note: Virtual pipe model (O'Brien and Hodgins 1995; Mei et al. 2007) on 0.5 m cells. stepS: fixed step in real seconds per tier; maxSteps per frame. friction: c_f per second; thinFriction adds drag on sheets under thinDepthM so thin films stop sliding. maxSpeed clamps velocity. manningN: Manning roughness of the ground (0.03 smooth earth channel, 0.05 grass); it caps flow speed by depth and slope, so thin water runs slowly and stays visible. dryDepthM: below this a cell counts as dry.
sim.prefillNote: At start, hollows deeper than prefillMinDepthM and larger than prefillMinAreaM2 begin full to their lip (until the water summary arrives in S4b). The starter spring lives in the land recipe.

summary.note: The deterministic water summary (docs/07): integers only, rebuilt after terrain edits, spring changes and once a game day, read by ecology and used as the live refill target. Spring-fed hollows always fill to their lip. Rain-fed: a dry hollow becomes a pond when at least pondMinCatchmentM2 and at least rainCatchmentRatio times its own full area drains into it, and it is at least pondMinDepthM deep at its deepest; it stands drawdownMaxM below its lip at most in late summer, never more than drawdownMaxFrac of its depth, rising and falling smoothly between drawdownDays (start, deepest, gone; days of the 56-day year from the first day of spring). Water table: a freshwater lens, at mean sea level along the shore and rising inland as tableMaxM sqrt(f (2 - f)), f the share of the way from the sea to the landmass's middle, tableSwingM lower at the deepest drawdown; a hollow whose floor lies at least tableMinDepthM under it fills to it (or to its lip), and it holds rain-fed ponds up. Other hollows stay damp. Stream depth d = clamp(streamK Q^streamExp, streamMinM, streamMaxM) with Q in L/s, capped by Manning depth for the local slope (manningN) over width w = streamW0 + streamW1 sqrt(Q). Classes by speed: still under slowSpeed, slow under runningSpeed, running above. bandFactor: the tide band is +-bandFactor A0 about mean sea level (the full spring range); splashFactor: the shore (graded shore height, docs/future/10) reaches this many A0 above the band top, for the splash zone. debounceS after a stroke before rebuilding.

nudge.note: Live water is topped up toward the summary target: d += (target - d)(1 - exp(-dt / tauS)) where d < target. Ponds refill and dug hollows that count as ponds fill to their lip in about a minute. Where a pond or stream stands above its target (a rain-fed pond lowering in summer), it evaporates toward it far more slowly, over evaporateTauH game hours, so the level eases down and never visibly drains; paused time stops it.

foam.note: Foam on the live water (docs/07, water-foam.wgsl, drawn in water-draw.wgsl). A coverage field on the 0.5 m cells, carried by the current and fading over fadeS; on still water (slower than stillBelowMs) it spreads out at spreadPerS (a share of the neighbors' average per second) and lingers for fadeStillS. Its lace rides the current through a flow map of flowCycleS, each spot resetting at its own moment, sliding at most maxSlideM a cycle (fast water churns instead of smearing). Made at falls: where the surface drops more than fallFromM into the neighbor the water flows toward, fallGain cover per meter of extra drop per second (full at 0.3 m/s or faster); where flows meet: convergenceGain cover per unit of convergence (1/s) per second; churn (stream riffles, beach swash; this replaced S4a's separate riffle flecks): churnGain cover per second where water is shallower than churnDepthM, fading in over the churnSpeed range (m/s). maxCover caps it. Drawing: lace breaks the cover into bubbly froth of laceM cells that boils in place at boil cells per second (no reset cycle, so nothing blinks); opacity is the most of a pixel foam covers; albedo is the foam's whiteness, lit like a rough surface.
foam.plungeNote: Where a waterfall lands (a neighbor whose bed stands more than plungeFromM higher sends water into this cell), plungeGain cover per second per m2/s of inflow (depth times speed toward this cell).

falls.note: Waterfalls (M2 Cliff tool; src/render/passes/falls.js, water-falls.wgsl). Visual only: the live sim still moves the water. Each frame a compute pass finds lips: water cells deeper than minDepthM flowing faster than minSpeedMs toward a neighbor whose bed lies more than minDropM lower. The edge is found by marching the ground from the cell in lipStepM steps up to lipReachM. Each lip draws a curtain from the edge along a gravity arc thrown out at the water's own speed, offsetM clear of the rock, widthScale x 0.5 m wide so neighbors overlap. Flow q (m2/s, depth x speed) sets the look: from threads at qThreadsM2s to a full sheet at qSheetM2s. Streaks are fixed in the time the water left the lip, so they fall at the true, quickening speed; streakM across, streakRateHz along. albedo: aerated water's whiteness, lit like a rough surface; opacity: the most of a pixel a full sheet covers. Spray: past sprayFromM2s, sprayPuffs soft puffs per lip rise at the foot, sprayM across, sprayOpacity at most. The water mesh hides its triangles steeper than hideWallDeg where a curtain falls. Caps and rows per tier in quality-tiers.json fallsMax, fallsRows. `?falls=0` turns waterfalls off.
falls.thicknessNote: The curtain is three layers through the water's body (back, middle, front, each with its own streaks; the outer ends round over). At the lip it is as thick as the water runs (flow / speed); over bulkM of drop it takes in air and bulks out to thicknessM, the first for a thread, the second for a full sheet.
falls.brinkNote: Water leaves a brink at about the critical speed sqrt(g x depth) (a 2 cm film at 0.44 m/s, 20 cm at 1.4 m/s): brinkShare of it, never more than the sim's own speed. Each lip's arc is followed down until it meets the ground or water under it; the curtain reaches tuckM past that, into the ground or the plunge.
falls.soundNote: For the sound of the falls (src/world/falls-near.js, audio/game.json falls): every soundReadS seconds the first soundLips lips found are read back from the GPU, a few kilobytes, mapped once the GPU is done so nothing waits on it.

fluid.note: Volumetric falls near the eye (src/render/passes/falls-fluid.js): screen-space fluid rendering (van der Laan, Green and Sainz 2009; Green, GDC 2010). Each lip within the tier's fallsFluid.nearM sends droplets off its edge, ratePerLipS a second at a full sheet and threadShare of that at a trickle (kept to a few threads), each radiusM, growing by bulk as it falls; they leave at the lip's brink speed, or fast enough to follow a leaning face down but never above maxLeanMs; fall under gravity with drag per second and spread by turbulence (m/s2); slide down steep rock; and are gone on reaching flat ground or water, or after about their fall time (never more than lifeS). Drawn as spheres into depth and thickness images (density x each sphere's depth through it); the depth is smoothed over widthM (at most maxPx pixels either way, across then down, iterations times), neighbors further than depthSigmaM in depth counting less; then shaded as water: the scene behind bent by refraction (screen uv per m of thickness) and dimmed by pond water's absorption, white in meandering ropes where aerated water (whitened over aerateS of falling) adds up to whiteThicknessM, lit at whiteAlbedo; ripples rippleM across running down at rippleSpeedMs tilt the surface by rippleTilt; glassy water mirrors the sky at roughness, times sheen, with sun glints at glintRoughness; thin edges fade in over edgeThicknessM. Drawn at the tier's fallsFluid.scale of the render size. Curtains give way to it over fadeM.

tools.note: Pour and drain (water tool) add or remove water under the brush at up to rateLps at full strength. Springs: up to maxSprings placed by the player (sandbox now, the dragonflies' gift in normal play), each at one of the rates (L/s).

look.note: Water optics (docs/07). absorption: sigma_a per meter (Beer-Lambert) for sea and ponds; scatterAlbedo: single-scatter albedo of the water body; f0: Fresnel at normal incidence (n = 1.333); refraction: screen offset per unit normal tilt; edgeFadeM: where the water plane meets the bank, it fades in over this much water thickness (the last half cell toward a dry bank fades too); coherentDepthM: water thinner than the first value is a broken, rough film (grass and stones stand through it, reflection weak), reaching a full mirror-like surface by the second; glossyDepthM: moving water (faster than 0.05 m/s) turns glossy over this depth range, so a brook glints but a film of a few millimeters sliding over grass does not; sheetDepthM: water thinner than the first value shows only as damp ground (the terrain soaks it), fully water by the second; waves: detail normal layers (wavelength m, strength, speed m/s); sea: Gerstner waves on open water (wavelength m, amplitude m, direction deg), faded out in water shallower than seaFadeDepthM, and on the sea only (never a pond, however deep). freshRipples: still fresh water (a pond, a marsh) is calm; its share of the waves layers goes from calm in still air to wind in a full wind (the weather's wind 0..1), while moving water stays choppy where a stream feeds it.

marshWater.note: Shallow, still fresh water among drowned plants (a marsh, a pond's shallow margin) holds much more dissolved peat than open pond water, so it reads darker and tea-brown and the sky's reflection shows on it. absorption: sigma_a per meter (Beer-Lambert), blue most; it gives way to absorptionPond over depthM and clears over stillMps of current.

look.pondNote: Pond water is peaty and a little cloudy: dissolved peat (tannins) absorbs blue strongly, water itself absorbs red, so the bed tints green-brown within a few tens of centimeters; fine silt scatters a soft olive glow (scatterAlbedoPond). The sea keeps absorptionSea and scatterAlbedo.
look.dampHollowNote: How wet the summary's damp hollows look (0 dry, 1 as soaked as a stream bank); hollows smaller than dampHollowMinM2 stay plain.

reflection.note: Island reflection (screen-space, high tiers; steps per tier in quality-tiers.json waterSSR). reachM: farthest a reflected ray looks for the island; thicknessM: how far behind a surface a ray may pass and still count as hitting it (grows 4% with distance); edgeFade: screen-edge fade width (uv); roughFade: water roughness range over which it gives way to the sky alone; startM: first step off the surface; rippleTilt: share of the ripple tilt the reflected ray follows (1 full: blotchy; lower: the bank wobbles but hangs together).

caustics.note: Caustics on underwater ground (docs/07, lib-caustics.wgsl), computed physically: a small rippled surface (waves: count plane waves in scattered directions, wavelengths spread between wavelengthM, each bending light equally (slope: the shortest wave's peak slope; longer waves are taller in proportion), moving at speedShare of real water-wave speed, directions jittered by directionJitterDeg around golden-angle steps) bends the sunlight entering it, and the light on the bed scales with 1 / |det(I + k Hessian)|, k = depth x 0.25 x focusGain. Ripples that curve like lenses gather light into soft bright filaments; the rest dims a little. They multiply direct sun and moon light only, so they vanish in shadow. strength: how far the light follows the computed focus (0 none, 1 full). softFloor and softPerM soften |det| so folds are filaments, not spikes, and deeper water blurs. Depth: faded in over fadeInM, shallowContrast of the contrast at the end of that fade rising to full at peakM, faded out over fadeOutM. projection: how far the pattern shifts along the light with depth (1: refraction at n = 1.333). flowDrift: share of the water speed the pattern drifts with; flowPeriodS: the flow map's cycle. minFinestPx: the caustics fade out once the shortest wave spans fewer pixels than this, so nothing shimmers far away Quality tier causticLayers: 2 sums all the waves, 1 drops the finest 40%, 0 off; ?caustics=0 turns them off.

ripples.note: Ripples (docs/07, src/world/water/ripples.js, water-ripples.wgsl): a damped 2D wave equation h' = (2h - h_prev + C^2 lap h) x damping, C = waveSpeed x substepS / texelM, on a window of size[tier] texels of texelM meters centered on the camera focus, stepped every substepS real seconds (at most maxSubsteps a frame). waveSpeed: ring speed (m/s; capillary-gravity ripples are about 0.23). fadeS: rings fall to 5% over this time (plus their own spreading). Held at rest where the live water is thinner than minWaterDepthM, fading in to full by three times that, so rings stop at the shore. Drops are smooth dips (1 - t^2)^2 of radiusM and strengthM (dip depth, m) pressed into the water at rest. rain: dropsPerM2S at full rain (the weather's rain is 0.1 to 0.6). pour: dropsPerS over the brush at full strength; brushRadiusM if the app gives none. impulse: defaults for addImpulse (frogs, fish). Rain and pour drops fall on a world grid of dropCellM cells, at most one per cell per substep; drop radii are capped at dropCellM. normalStrength scales the slope added to the water normal; edgeFadeM fades it out toward the window edge.

rain.note: Unused since raindrops became rings in the water shader (rings below); kept so the ripple field can still take rain if wanted.

rings.note: Raindrop rings drawn in water-draw.wgsl (finer than the ripple field holds): drops fall on cellM cells, each lasting lifeS while its ring spreads to radiusM; crests crestM apart with peak slope `slope`; maxShare of the cells hold a drop at full rain. They fade where a pixel is too coarse for the crests.
